title: On The Variability of Concept Activation Vectors
abstract: arXiv:2509.24058v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: One of the most pressing challenges in artificial intelligence is to make models more transparent to their users. Recently, explainable artificial intelligence has come up with numerous methods to tackle this challenge. A promising avenue is to use concept-based explanations, that is, high-level concepts instead of plain feature importance scores. Among this class of methods, Concept Activation Vectors (CAVs, Kim et al., 2018) stand out as one of the main protagonists. One interesting aspect of CAVs is that their computation requires sampling random examples from the train set. Therefore, the actual vectors obtained may vary depending on the randomness of this sampling. In this paper, we propose a fine-grained theoretical analysis of CAV construction in order to quantify their variability. Our results, confirmed by experiments on several real-life datasets of four different modalities, point to an universal result: the variance

translated_title: 论概念激活向量的变异性
translated_abstract: 人工智能中最紧迫的挑战之一是让模型对用户更加透明。近年来，可解释人工智能领域提出了众多方法来应对这一挑战。一个有前景的方向是使用基于概念的解释，即采用高层概念而非简单的特征重要性分数。在这类方法中，概念激活向量（CAVs，Kim et al., 2018）脱颖而出，成为其中的代表性方法之一。CAV的一个有趣之处在于，其计算需要从训练集中随机采样样本。因此，实际得到的向量可能因这种随机采样的不确定性而有所不同。在本文中，我们对CAV的构建提出了细粒度的理论分析，以量化其变异性。我们的结果在四种不同模态的多个真实数据集上的实验中得到验证，指向一个普适性结论：其方差……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 本文对概念激活向量（CAV）的构建过程进行了细粒度的理论分析，量化了其因训练集随机采样而产生的变异性，并在四种不同模态的真实数据集上通过实验验证了结果的普适性。
en_tdlr: This paper provides a fine-grained theoretical analysis of Concept Activation Vector (CAV) construction to quantify its variability arising from random sampling of training examples, with the results validated by experiments on real-life datasets of four different modalities.
